title: Psychometrics in Inspera - Our Strategy
text: This Quicksight Dashboard is part of phase 1 in our strategy for Introducing Test-Level Analysis in Inspera Higher Education Institutions. Further details regarding our strategy and phasing are described in the following sections. ## Background Inspera currently offers advanced analytics exclusively for clients in another market segment using item banks and Item Response Theory (IRT) through Inspera’s GIRT-engine (Generalised Item Response Theory). These clients, primarily awarding bodies, deliver standardised tests within Inspera, with the analytics enabling them to conduct detailed item-level analysis both directly within the Inspera platform and through our Data Discovery Tool, which offers advanced filtering capabilities for in-depth data exploration. However, this IRT-based approach is not directly applicable to our traditional Higher Education customers. Typically, HE institutions do not utilise item banks in the same way as awarding bodies, as they have different needs regarding content creation, permission control, and metadata services (we are currently working on adapting item banks within Inspera to better cater to these HE requirements). Furthermore, HE institutions tend to rely on Classical Test Theory (CTT) for test analysis because they need to analyse data at the test level or within the context of a single test, rather than a strong focus on individual question level. In contrast, awarding bodies’ assessment model generates individual test versions for each test taker, rendering test-level analysis across versions impractical. This necessitates a focus on analysing individual question performance across all test versions. Therefore, to better serve our HE users, we are expanding our analytics to include CTT-based test-centric analysis, moving beyond the current focus on individual questions. Below, we outline our roadmap and staged approach to build this new capability, crucially incorporating client feedback at each stage to ensure a product that meets your needs. ## Vision for Test-Level Analysis in Inspera Building upon our existing

title: Psychometrics Dashboard - Overview
text: This is a guide to psychometrics at Inspera, provided in the form of a dashboard. This is a crucial first step in bringing comprehensive test-level analytics. It is designed specifically for educators, administrators, and analysts involved in creating, delivering, and evaluating assessments for Higher Education institution. This dashboard was developed to: - Provide HE clients with access to key CTT-based test statistics and visualizations. - Gather essential feedback on the most valuable test statistic graphs and visualizations. - Prototype and refine test-level analytics features before integrating them directly into the Inspera platform. ## Understanding the Visualisations and the Data Click on the individual graphs to get a more detailed explanation. ### 1. Test Summary Metrics This summary provides key statistical summaries of test performance, including student participation, score distribution, and reliability, offering a quick snapshot of the overall test results. ### 2. Student Response Trends This graph breaks down student responses per question into exposed, answered, omitted, and unexposed categories. Use it to quickly assess student engagement and spot trends in how questions were attempted or skipped ### 3. Total Score Distribution See how many students achieved each specific total score on the test. This graph highlights the overall performance distribution, showing the range from lowest to highest scores and which scores were most common. ### 4. Facility and Discrimination See how difficult each question was versus how well it distinguished between high and low-scoring students on this scatter plot. It provides a visual summary of question performance, helping to spot items that might need review or are working effectively. The dashboard also provides separate graphs if you want to analyze question difficulty or differentiation trends individually. ### 5. title: Psychometrics Dashboard - Getting Started
text: ## Data Considered for Calculation The dashboard includes data for automatically marked questions only. Manually marked questions and their scores are excluded. Additionally, the submission data syncs to the dashboard once every 24 hours. This includes data from tests that are still ongoing. To ensure all submissions are reflected, please wait up to 24 hours after the test's official end time before considering the data complete. ## Assessment Run ID Note : By default, the first view of the dashboard shows the psychometrics for all tests. In this view, you may see an overwhelming number of data points, incorrect order of questions, etc.This may also happen if you reset your dashboard to its original settings. We advise you to select a specific Assessment Run ID to view the data for a specific test as explained in this section. The next time you view the dashboard, QuickSight remembers your last selected ID and shows the the corresponding data. The dashboard displays metrics for a single test at a time. To view a specific test on the dashboard, you must enter its Assessment Run ID into the designated input field. This field is primarily for quickly switching between tests where you already know the Assessment Run ID. It is not designed to search for unknown Assessment Run IDs. ## Finding the Assessment Run ID To find the Assessment Run ID: - Navigate to the "Deliver" module within Inspera. - Locate and open the specific test. - The Assessment Run ID is the number at theendof the URL in your browser's address bar. - Enter this number into the dashboard's input field. ## Understanding Question Numbering Many graphs in the dashboard visualise metrics (e.g., facility, average time spent) as a function of question number. However, the "question number" displayed might not always directly

text: number at theendof the URL in your browser's address bar. - Enter this number into the dashboard's input field. ## Understanding Question Numbering Many graphs in the dashboard visualise metrics (e.g., facility, average time spent) as a function of question number. However, the "question number" displayed might not always directly correspond to the question numbering you see within the Inspera assessment. This is because a single question can have more than one interaction. Multiple Interactions within a Single Question Inspera allows you to create a single question (of type "Multiple Choice," for example) that contains multipleinteractions. An interaction is a single, answerable element within a question. See the image below for an example. Example: Consider a short test with three questions visible in the Inspera navigation bar. Question 2, however, is a question containingtwomultiple-choice interactions. This means: - The student must answerfourdistinct questions in total. - The Psychometrics dashboard will display data forfourquestions, treating each interaction as a separate question. Important Note about Time Spent: If multiple questions (interactions) are displayed on the same page within Inspera, they willalwaysshare the same average time spent. This is because the system cannot determine precisely which interaction a student is actively working on when multiple interactions are presented simultaneously. Therefore the time spent cannot be calculated per question.

title: Psychometrics Dashboard - FAQ
text: Q: When is the data for my test available on the dashboard? A:Submission data syncs to the dashboard once every 24 hours. This includes data from tests that are still ongoing. To ensure all submissions are reflected, please wait up to 24 hours after the test's official end time before considering the data complete. Currently the data is updated 10.15 UTC. Q. What types of tests are supported in the dashboard? A:At the moment, assessments which have enabled multiple attempts are not supported. Hence, even if you enter their Assessment Run ID in the dropdown, you would get no results. Q: What question types are supported? A:The dashboard includes data forautomatically marked questions only. Manually marked questions and their scores are excluded. Q: The question numbering is not as expected, what could be the reason? A:This can happen if a single question contains multiple parts (interactions). The dashboard lists each interaction as a separate question for analysis, affecting the apparent order and total count. Stimulus materials will alter the numbering. They're numbered internally by dashboard but not shown. For example, if question 1 has a document stimulus it will appear as question 2 on the dashboard and question 1 (the stimulus) will be hidden. This is a known issue that we are working to address. Q: I have found a quality issue with a question, how do I look up the question in Inspera? A:Use the Assessment Run ID to go directly to the test event in the Deliver module via this URL format (replace placeholders and ensure you're logged into Inspera Admin):https://<your_inspera_domain>/admin/#deliver-test/<Assessment Run ID>Once there Preview the Question Set and navigate to the question. Q: Will the dashboard be accessible via an API for custom analysis? A:Today, psychometrics data is only available in the form of a QuickSight dashboard.

title: Psychometrics Dashboard - 1. Test Summary Metrics
text: At the test level, these metrics provide a comprehensive view of student performance and the reliability of the assessment. The metrics are: - Students Enrolled- The total number of students who were enrolled in the test. - Students Submitted- The total number of students who successfully submitted the test. - Score Standard Deviation- Measures the variability of scores around the mean. A higher value signifies greater variability in scores, visually represented in the Total Score Distribution graph. - Minimum Score- The minimum score obtained on the test. - Mean Score- The mean score obtained on the test. - Maximum Score- The maximum score obtained on the test. - Cronbach's Alpha- This metric measures the internal consistency of a test, specifically how well a set of test questions work together to assess a single, unified concept. The value of Cronbach's Alpha should range between 0 and 1. A value of 0.7 or higher is generally considered acceptable, indicating good internal consistency.However, if a test is designed to measure multiple distinct skills or concepts, a lower Cronbach's Alpha is expected. For example, a math test focusing solely on algebra would typically exhibit a higher Cronbach's Alpha than an entrance exam measuring diverse skills like language comprehension, logical reasoning, and spatial awareness.A value close to 0 indicates no consistency among the test items. While theoretically possible, a negative Cronbach's Alpha suggests severe problems with the test questions, requiring immediate review.https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cronbach%27s_alpha

title: Psychometrics Dashboard - 2. Students Response Trends
text: This graph presents a detailed breakdown of student response patterns for each question on a recent test. It utilises a grouped bar chart to display the counts of four distinct response categories: 'Exposed' (students viewed the question), 'Answered' (students provided an answer), 'Omitted' (students skipped the question), and 'Unexposed' (students did not reach the question). Because the questions are presented in sequential order, this visualisation allows for the identification of trends in student behaviour throughout the test. For instance, it can reveal patterns of question skipping, indicating potential areas of difficulty or confusion. Furthermore, by examining the 'Unexposed' data, it becomes possible to assess whether students had sufficient time to complete the entire test. This analysis provides valuable insights into student engagement and test-taking strategies. ### Metrics - Exposed- The total number of students who saw a question (The question was loaded on their browser). This number does not consider students who were initially enrolled in the test but did not start the test. - Answered- The total number of students to whom a question was exposed, and who provided some answer to the question. - Omitted- The total number of students to whom a question was exposed, but they did not attempt an answer. - Unexposed- The total number of students who did not see a question (The question was not loaded on their browser). This number does not consider students who were initially enrolled in the test but did not start the test.

title: Psychometrics Dashboard - 3. Total Score Distribution
text: ## Total score distribution and table list This chart presents the distribution of student total scores for the selected test. A bar graph visually displays the frequency of each score achieved, while an accompanying table lists one entry per student, showing the user ID and their corresponding score, ordered from lowest to highest score. This visualisation provides an overview of the score distribution, revealing the minimum, maximum, and most common scores, thus highlighting the overall performance range and scoring patterns for this specific test. Furthermore, the distribution can indicate whether the test was potentially too easy or too difficult. A concentration of scores towards the higher end suggests an easier test, while a concentration towards the lower end suggests a more challenging one. ### Metrics - Total score- The overall score achieved by a student on a test - Frequency- The number of students who achieved that score. ## Box Plot of Total Score Distribution Complementing the score frequency bar chart, a box plot provides a concise visual summary of the total score distribution. The central box represents the interquartile range (IQR), encompassing the middle 50% of scores, from the 25th percentile (Q1) to the 75th percentile (Q3). The line within the box marks the median score. Whiskers extend to the minimum and maximum scores, illustrating the typical spread of data while excluding potential outliers. This box plot offers a compressed yet detailed view of score distributions, allowing for quick identification of central tendency, spread, and potential outliers, thus enhancing the understanding of the test's overall performance profile. ### Metrics - TOTALSCORE (Max):The highest score obtained. - TOTALSCORE (Q3):The 75th percentile, indicating that 75% of scores fall below this value. - TOTALSCORE (Median):The middle score of the distribution. - TOTALSCORE (Q1):The 25th percentile, indicating that 25% of scores fall below

title: Psychometrics Dashboard - 4. Facility and Discrimination
text: ## Facility vs Discrimination by question number This scatter plot visualises the relationship between questionfacilityanddiscriminationfor a given test. The plot allows for the identification of trends and outliers in question difficulty, and the detection of poorly discriminating questions, which may signal issues with answer keys or question design. On hover, you can view the facility and discrimination values, along with the question number. ### Metrics - Facility (x-axis):Represents the difficulty of a question, ranging from 0 to 1. A lower value indicates a more difficult question. It's calculated as the proportion of correct responses to total attempts, normalised to 1. - Discrimination (y-axis):Indicates how effectively a question differentiates between high-performing and low-performing students, ranging from -1 to +1. A value of 0 suggests no differentiation, while negative values indicate that higher-performing students are more likely to answer incorrectly (potentially due to an error in the answer key). For more information, please refer to the point-biserial correlation coefficient. ### Interpreting the Quadrants: - Upper Right:Questions that are relatively easy and effectively differentiate between students. - Upper Left:Questions that are challenging but still provide valuable discrimination. - Lower Right:Questions that are easy but offer limited differentiation. - Lower Left:Questions that are difficult and poorly discriminating, indicating potential problems. - Negative Discrimination:Raises a red flag and warrants immediate investigation. Important Note:While this graph is not currently showing very easy questions, it is important to remember that both very easy and very difficult questions often exhibit low discrimination. This is due to the inherent nature of these questions: most students will either answer them correctly (very easy) or incorrectly (very difficult), resulting in limited differentiation. ## Facility by question number As explained earlier, facility represents the difficulty of a question, ranging from 0 to 1. title: Psychometrics Dashboard - 5. Mean Score and Facility Distribution by Question Type
text: These two graphs, which present data on question type performance, are displayed side-by-side within the dashboard ## Mean Score Distribution by Question Type This bar chart illustrates the average scores achieved for each automatically marked question type within the test. TheMean Scoremetric represents the average score of all students who attempted questions of a particular type. This visualization helps to identify performance trends across different question formats, highlighting which question types students found relatively easier or more challenging. ## Mean Facility Distribution by Question Type This bar chart displays the mean facility (difficulty) levels for each question type. The 'Mean Facility' metric reflects the average facility of all questions belonging to a specific type. This provides valuable insights into the relative difficulty of various question formats, indicating which question types were generally easier or more difficult for the student cohort.

title: Psychometrics Dashboard - 6. Average Time Per Question
text: Understanding how students allocate their time during a test is crucial for assessing its effectiveness. This graph provides a detailed view of the average time spent on each question, complementing the 'Students response trends' analysis by revealing potential time management challenges. This graph presents the average time, measured in seconds, that students spent answering each question in the assessment. A bar chart visually displays this data, while an accompanying table lists the average duration for each question. The 'Avg duration (seconds)' metric represents the mean time taken across all students who were exposed to a particular question. This visualization allows for: - Evaluation of time spent on each question:Identifying questions where students spend significantly more or less time. - Identification of questions requiring disproportionate time:Highlighting potential issues with question clarity, complexity, or length. The data is ordered sequentially by question number, mirroring the test's structure. When viewed alongside the 'Students response trends' graph, this analysis offers a comprehensive understanding of student behaviour, revealing whether time constraints or question difficulty influenced response patterns, such as question skipping or incomplete sections.

title: Psychometrics Dashboard - 7. Question Metrics Table
text: This table presents a detailed summary of question-level metrics, offering a granular view of each question's performance and psychometric properties. It is located at the bottom of the dashboard for easy access and reference For further analysis or reporting, the data within this table can be easily exported in both CSV and Excel formats. This allows you to manipulate and analyze the question metrics using your preferred spreadsheet software. ### Columns - Question Number:The sequential number of the question as it appeared in the test. - Question ID:A unique identifier for the question. - Mean Score:The average score achieved on the question. - Discrimination:How well the question differentiates between high and low-performing students. - Facility:The difficulty level of the question, represented as the proportion of students who answered correctly. - Exposed:The number of students who viewed the question. - Unexposed:The number of students who did not reach the question. - Answered:The number of students who provided an answer to the question. - Omitted:The number of students who skipped the question.
